**Self-governance** — governing oneself by standards that are one's own — identification and wholeheartedness, planning agency and policies, self-constitution, autonomy and authenticity, and the empirical psychology of self-endorsed motives. One of four unities kept apart (group: philosophy; ADR-024).

| [TERM-053](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-053.md) | endorsement, between an organization's processes: any effect one process has on another's share of future influence, of which an explicit vote is one case | The owner's "vote" at U2, generalized at A5 §7 to an effective causal relation. | [TERM-060](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-060.md) | frustration, of an organization's demands: the failure of the demands it maintains to be jointly realizable under its admissible transformations and its governance | A33 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, at the owner's U33, made ordinal by the owner's U37 correction. The demands an organization maintains are frustrated when no admissible transformation meets them all (structural) or when one exists and the organization's governance does not select it (governance-induced). In its basic form it is an empty intersection of acceptance sets and needs no common scale. It is distinct from strain, where the demands are jointly realizable at a cost, and from distress, a possible integrated response to either. It is not [CLAIM-153](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md)'s physics sense, though it shares that sense's three-demand minimal obstruction. | Active |

[TERM-050](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-050.md)'s sense, all regimes ranking the same course first, is not a special case of it: agreement in rankings needs no coupling, and coupling needs no agreement.
